    • at

      public MKCContainerPanel.Builder at(Supplier<ScreenOrigin> origin, int padding)
      Pixel-precision placement (§0057 Revision — Trev's call, 2026-07-01): the panel's outer top-left comes from origin, re-evaluated every frame, in absolute screen pixels. The precision escape for the positions regions cannot express — a point inside the content frame (e.g. a panel directly above the offhand slot, via VanillaSlotResolver.resolve(AbstractContainerScreen, int)) or an origin that moves per frame (e.g. a row centred over the hovered hotbar column). Returning null skips the panel that frame — the natural "this screen doesn't surface my anchor" escape.

      Everything else about the parity panel is unchanged: the slots are real synced MKCSlots on every container menu, the chrome + SlotElements ride the panel (their intra-panel offsets are fixed; only the panel origin moves), and parity(ScreenMatcher)/showWhen(BooleanSupplier) compose as usual. No reactive wrap/scroll budgets are fed — pixel placement means the consumer owns the exact geometry, on-screen included.

      Mutually exclusive with the region .at(...) overloads — declare exactly one placement.

      Parameters:
      origin - per-frame supplier of the panel's outer top-left in absolute screen pixels; null return = skip frame
      padding - content padding inside the panel edge (often 0 for slot-tight precision panels)

    • parity

      public MKCContainerPanel.Builder parity(ScreenMatcher scope)
      Screen scope for the panel's presentation. Default ScreenMatcher.all() — shown on every container screen. Opt a screen out with ScreenMatcher.allExcept(Class...). Does NOT affect where the slot data lives (that's every container menu); see the class doc.

    • chrome

      public MKCContainerPanel.Builder chrome(Supplier<List<PanelElement>> chrome)
      The panel's display elements (buttons, labels, decorations), built lazily on the client only. The slots are added automatically as SlotElements from addSlot(SlotSpec); this supplies the rest of the panel's chrome. MUST NOT be invoked on a dedicated server — it isn't (the library calls it client-side from MKCClient).

    • showWhen

      public MKCContainerPanel.Builder showWhen(BooleanSupplier visibleWhen)
      Gates the WHOLE panel's visibility (chrome + slot presentation) on a client-side predicate — the entire parity panel appears/disappears as one. Default (unset): always visible. When the supplier returns false, the chrome, background, and slot elements all stop rendering together; per-group revealWhen still applies on top when the panel is shown. Client-side presentation gate (the underlying Panel.showWhen(BooleanSupplier)); does not by itself drive server slot-sync, so pair it with per-group revealWhen when the slots are sync-critical (as the validator pool does).

    • pinnedHeight

      public MKCContainerPanel.Builder pinnedHeight(int h)
      Pins the panel's height to a fixed pixel extent (default: auto-size to visible content). Use when the panel is bottom/right-anchored AND its visible content fluctuates between frames — e.g. a group revealed by a per-frame revealWhen predicate. Without a pin, an anchored panel's auto-size changes when a group reveals, which moves the already-visible slots; if a reveal predicate reads cursor-over-slot state, that motion can un-trigger the reveal and oscillate (a flash). Pinning the height reserves the panel's full extent so reveals never shift existing slots. Mirrors Panel.pinnedHeight(int); width stays adaptive.
      Parameters:
      h - pinned content height in pixels

    • pinnedWidth

      public MKCContainerPanel.Builder pinnedWidth(int w)
      Pins the panel's width to a fixed pixel extent (default: auto-size to visible content). The width twin of pinnedHeight(int) — and the one that matters for a RIGHT-anchored, hover-reveal panel: when a revealed group is WIDER than the already-visible ones, an adaptive width grows the panel, and a right anchor turns that growth into a LEFTWARD shift of the existing slots. If the reveal predicate reads cursor-over-slot state, that shift slides the hover target out from under the cursor and oscillates (the flash). Pinning the width reserves the panel's full horizontal extent so reveals never shift existing slots sideways. Mirrors Panel.pinnedWidth(int).
      Parameters:
      w - pinned content width in pixels

    • register

      public void register()
      Finalises the registration. Side-neutral: registers each slot recipe, ensures the foreign-menu projection source exists, and stores the definition for client chrome wiring. Call once at mod init (common initializer).
